title: What is a mutual fund?
objectives: Explain in two minutes how a mutual fund pools money and who does what.
Name the sponsor, trustees, AMC, custodian and RTA and say who holds the investor's money.
Say why a unit price (NAV) moves with the market.
body_md:
A mutual fund pools money from many investors and invests it in shares, bonds and other securities as set out in each scheme's mandate. Each investor owns **units** in proportion to the money put in, so everyone shares the gains, losses and costs in the same proportion.

## Who does what

| Entity | Role | What it means for the client |
|---|---|---|
| SEBI | Regulator for mutual funds and intermediaries | Rules on categories, costs, disclosures and investor protection |
| Sponsor and Trust / Trustees | The sponsor sets up the fund; trustees protect unitholders' interests | An independent layer watches the fund house |
| AMC (fund house) | Manages the money as per each scheme's mandate | The fund manager decides what to buy within the scheme's rules |
| Custodian | Holds the fund's securities | Investor money is not held by the AMC or the distributor |
| RTA (CAMS / KFintech) | Keeps investor records, processes transactions, issues statements | Where folios, nominations and service requests are processed |
| AMFI | Industry body; registers distributors (ARN) | Runs investor awareness and the distributor code of conduct |
| Distributor (Fund Horizon) | Helps the client choose, invest, review and stay invested | Earns trail commission from the AMC; never handles client money |

## Three ideas to remember

- **Units, not shares.** A client buys units at the scheme's NAV. Buying more units when the price is low and fewer when high is how a SIP works.
- **Pooling gives access.** A client with ₹500 gets the same diversified portfolio as one with ₹5 crore, scaled down.
- **Risk is not removed.** A mutual fund is subject to market risk. Diversification reduces single-stock risk; it does not remove market risk.

> **Investor takeaway:** Your money sits with a custodian in a regulated structure, and you hold units in your own name.
example: Four friends put ₹10,000 each into a fund when its NAV is ₹20. Each gets 500 units. If the NAV rises to ₹22, each holding is worth ₹11,000, and each owns exactly a quarter of the scheme's gain.
say: Your money sits with the fund's custodian, not with us.
A mutual fund invests across many securities. It is still subject to market risk.
never: Your money is safe with a mutual fund.
We hold your money and invest it for you.

check.q: Who holds the securities of a mutual fund scheme?
check.why: An independent custodian holds the fund's securities. Investor money is never held by the AMC or the distributor.

check.q: Which body registers mutual fund distributors and issues the ARN?
check.why: AMFI is the industry body that registers distributors (ARN). SEBI is the regulator.

check.q: Four investors each put in ₹10,000 at the same NAV. The NAV then rises 10%. What happens to each holding?
o: The AMC keeps part of the gain
It stays the same until redemption
check.why: All unitholders share gains, losses and costs in proportion to their units.
